title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
subtitle: scrambled egg with ripe tomatoes, sugar and sesame oil
excerpt: A Chinese home-cooking staple of silky scrambled egg combined with tomatoes cooked down to a light, sweet-savoury sauce. Ready in 20 minutes and eaten over rice. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Xihongshi chao jidan (tomato and egg stir-fry) is arguably the most universally cooked dish in Chinese home cooking, recognised across all regions and generations. Tomatoes arrived in China via Portuguese and Spanish traders in the sixteenth century and were gradually incorporated into Chinese cooking over the following centuries. By the twentieth century, the tomato and egg combination was a fixture of home kitchens throughout China, documented in popular Chinese cookbooks from the 1950s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: Literally 'breath of the wok'. The slightly smoky, charred aroma that develops when food is cooked over very high heat in a well-seasoned wok. Achieved at home by getting the wok as hot as possible before adding oil.

A dark, fragrant oil pressed from toasted sesame seeds. Used as a finishing condiment rather than a cooking oil, as its flavour diminishes under direct heat. A small amount adds a characteristic nutty aroma.
A Chinese rice wine with a nutty, amber flavour used widely in marinades, sauces and braises. Named after the city of Shaoxing in Zhejiang province. Dry sherry is the closest substitute.

Cook the eggs first, then remove them and cook the tomatoes separately. Cooking both together makes the egg rubbery. The two components reunite only at the very end of cooking.

items.prepNote: beaten with 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and a pinch of salt

content.text: Beat the eggs with 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, a pinch of salt and a pinch of white pepper if you have it.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the wok over high heat. Pour in the eggs and scramble gently until just set but still slightly underdone. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok. Add the garlic and fry for 20 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing them lightly with a spatula, until they have collapsed and released their juice.
Add the sugar, soy sauce and the remaining 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine. Stir to combine.
Return the egg to the wok. Toss gently for 30 seconds until the egg and tomatoes are combined and the egg is just cooked through.
Drizzle with sesame oil and scatter with spring onions. Serve immediately over steamed rice.

items.cause: Overcooked, or cooked together with the tomatoes.
items.fix: Remove the egg while it is still slightly underdone. It will finish cooking when it goes back in the wok.

items.cause: Cooked over too low a heat or not long enough.
items.fix: Use ripe tomatoes and cook over high heat, pressing with the spatula until they break down and thicken.

items.cause: Not enough sugar or the tomatoes were underripe.
items.fix: Add another half teaspoon of sugar, or a splash of rice vinegar to sharpen the flavour.

content.text: Tomato and egg stir-fry is often the first dish a Chinese child learns to cook and the last thing eaten when there is nothing left in the fridge. It is eaten across every region of China without meaningful variation: eggs, tomatoes, a little sugar, a little soy, sesame oil. The fact that it works so reliably from so few ingredients explains why it has remained a constant of Chinese home cooking across generations.
